name: Buddy
subtitle: Buddy, your AI helper in the Dynamic Island

apps.name: Buddy
apps.subtitle: Ask anything from the Dynamic Island
apps.localizedDescription: Buddy lives in your Dynamic Island. Tap it to ask, or double-tap the back of your iPhone to send a screenshot - the answer appears right in the island while you stay in your app. Free brain, no account.

versions.localizedDescription:
• A pointer named after the task or app flies to every window it opens (a browser, a command window, a mail page) and says what it is doing. When such a program steers a browser started with --remote-debugging-port, the pointer flies to every click and hops with a ripple. The pointer of an AI app goes away after a minute without news.
• A trace you can read: %APPDATA%\Buddy\crew\trace.log, one line for each start, window, click and end, with the time. Never what was typed or a web address; it stays on this PC.
• A button next to the clock (a green arrow when on, grey with a red bar when off): one click turns the pointers on or off, right-click opens the trace. Windows 10 puts a new icon behind the ^ arrow: drag it onto the taskbar once. The same from outside: Buddy.exe --pointers on|off|toggle.
• Off until you tick it: Buddy window, tab Settings, box Buddy's brain, Also show scheduled tasks and what AI apps open and A button next to the clock that switches all those pointers off or on with one click. It comes back by itself after Buddy restarts.
• This replaces the separate Task herald helper: nothing else to install or start.
• Never late. Each look at the open windows used to take 0.9 to 2 s (up to 8.4 s) when Buddy was busy, so a pointer could arrive after the window was already gone. A look now takes about 1 ms. Measured with the built app on a real screen for 30 minutes: no slow look (before: 9 looks of 1.1 to 8.4 s in 23 minutes); a new window is in the trace after 0.02 to 0.18 s (median 0.13 s, 10 tries); the pointer is on the new window after 0.18 to 0.90 s (median 0.45 s, 26 tries, 1 over 0.5 s).
• Checked on a real screen with the built app: pointers on windows opened by scheduled tasks and by an AI app, click animation in a steered Edge, the button and its right-click menu, both tick boxes, on/off from the command line, and that all of it is back after Buddy restarts.
• Not checked: clicks in browsers other than Edge, and a full Windows restart (Buddy starts with Windows as before, the restart itself was not tried). When the whole PC stops for a few seconds, the pointer waits too.
